ruleName: Ball rolls into your own footprints
group: Ball rolls into your own footprints
imagePrompt: A teen boy stands in a bunker, considering a shot to a ball that has settled in his own deep footprints.
imageAlt: Teen boy golfer in a bunker, looking down at a ball resting in his footprints.

issues: The boy's skin tone could be slightly more medium for a stronger 'mixed' appearance, but it is within reasonable range.
The footprints could be a bit deeper/more visually distinct to strengthen the context of the quiz scenario (ball in deep footprints).
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Increase the visibility and depth of the footprints around the ball to make it clear the ball is in the boy's own deep footprints. Slightly enhance the medium tone and mixed ethnicity appearance of the teen boy for greater clarity.

questions.title: Your Ball Stops in Your Own Footprints in the Sand
questions.question: You hit your golf ball from the bunker and it rolls back into the marks your feet made in the sand. What should you do?

choices.text: Smooth the sand where your ball stopped before you hit
Pick up your ball and put it somewhere else in the bunker for free
Hit the ball from the spot where it is, or say it is unplayable
Move your ball to a spot with smoother sand

questions.explanation: You have to play your ball from the footprints, or you can say it is unplayable and follow those rules. You cannot smooth the sand or move the ball to a nicer spot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A sandy area on the golf course, sometimes called a sand trap.
When you decide your ball is too hard to play, you can choose to take a penalty and drop it somewhere else by the rules.

questions.teachingTip: Ask the child to show how they would play a shot from rough sand, and talk about why the rule says to leave the sand how it is.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think it’s okay to smooth the sand before hitting the next shot.
They might believe they can always move their ball to a better spot in the bunker without penalty.

questions.title: Ball Rolls Back Into Your Footprints in Bunker
questions.question: After playing a shot from a bunker, your ball rolls back and comes to rest in the footprints you made. What are your options?

choices.text: Smooth out the footprints before your next shot
Play the ball as it lies or declare it unplayable
Move the ball to a nicer patch of sand

questions.explanation: You must play the ball as it lies, even if it is in your own footprints, unless you declare the ball unplayable under the rules.
